scenario: You are running Orchestrated Mode on a shipped pricing-calculator page (customer-facing, money). Walk through, step by step, how you pick the mode and round budget, and state exactly when a model:opus reviewer joins and how you know the round is clean. Then: it is round 6 and the last round found only Low findings. State the exact rule for whether you stop or continue.
decision_point: Stakes-to-mode table row for a customer-facing money surface; opus seat join timing (DEEP round 4+); clean-round stop rule at round 6 with only Low findings
pass_rule: Walk-through cites the exact rule, table row, or threshold from the file at each material decision point; quoting the file's own escalation-floor language counts as PASS.
fail_rule: Assumption language ('I'll assume', 'unclear whether'), a question addressed to the user, or a chosen action contradicting a rule in the file.

before_after.baseline_behavior: The pre-upgrade baseline (commit 371533a) has no 'Stakes-to-mode table', no explicit production/money/customer trigger for DEEP mode, and no orchestration-specific convergence rule at all: Orchestrated Mode existed but its stop conditions were just the generic base-mode 'When to stop' list (user says stop, all-Low round, 'you genuinely cannot identify meaningful improvements (be honest about this)', or five rounds completed with a suggestion to continue). There is also no rule anywhere about WHEN an opus critic seat joins; critics are simply '2 critic agents (Sonnet)' with no model-tier escalation language at all, and no data-fidelity third-seat trigger.
before_after.upgraded_behavior: The upgraded text adds a named Stakes-to-mode table that mechanically maps 'production/money/customer surfaces' to DEEP/cap-8, an explicit 'from round 4 onward, one of the two critic seats runs at model: opus' rule, an explicit orchestration-only convergence rule ('stop on a clean round... on the mode's round cap, or on thrash') that supersedes the generic base rule under orchestration ('Round caps are HARD under orchestration... The base suggest-stopping condition does not apply'), and a data-fidelity third-seat trigger tied to whether the work transforms data.
judgment_points_closed: Which mode applies to a given artifact (previously the agent had to eyeball 'is this important enough for Deep' with no named signal list; now a literal table row names 'production/money/customer surfaces')
Whether/when a stronger reviewer model joins a DEEP round (previously no escalation mechanism existed in Orchestrated Mode at all)

Whether an all-Low round at round 6 of 8 must keep going to reach the cap versus stop immediately (previously would have fallen back to the generic base rule's vaguer 'be honest about this' / suggest-stopping-but-offer-to-continue language, which is advisory rather than a hard stop)

Whether the base mode's soft 'suggest stopping, offer to continue' language even applies under orchestration (previously ambiguous since Orchestrated Mode didn't override it; now explicitly stated it does not apply, the director stops full stop)
Whether a third critic seat is needed when data is embedded/transformed (previously no such seat existed in the critic-count language at all)

result.evidence: Decision point: "shipped pricing-calculator page, customer-facing, money" -> mode/round-budget pick. Exact rule applied: the Orchestrated Mode "Stakes-to-mode table" row "Ship gates and production/money/customer surfaces | DEEP | 8, walking the Depth Ladder, until only Low remains" (SKILL.md line 286). Opus-join rule applied verbatim: "DEEP mode only: from round 4 onward, one of the two (or three) critic seats runs at model: opus instead of sonnet; keep the other seat(s) at sonnet" (line 288). Clean-round rule applied verbatim: "Convergence: stop on a clean round (no High or Medium findings), on the mode's round cap, or on thrash" (line 293), reinforced by line 295's "Deep at 8 (or earlier on a clean round)". Round-6-Low-only decision point resolved directly by that same convergence rule: a Low-only round is a clean round by definition, so it stops regardless of not having reached the round-8 cap. No line in my walk-through contains assumption language, no question was addressed to the user, and the stop-at-6 action is directly licensed (not contradicted) by the file's stated convergence rule.
